### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **106** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**75** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9d0772309f9b3879fbbb2d3f4008d6f97ed580da`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `resolveExecCtx (35 routes)`, `routeManager (25 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 41 pages)`
- **22** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **186** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9d0772309f9b3879fbbb2d3f4008d6f97ed580da` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `998730aa891d0819d10310cd42bcbe8ef6bc956b` — the merge of head `7928062332ebd43e587f6cbbb710dcd1b4f7df6c` into base `9d0772309f9b3879fbbb2d3f4008d6f97ed580da`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 998730aa891d0819d10310cd42bcbe8ef6bc956b && git checkout 998730aa891d0819d10310cd42bcbe8ef6bc956b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9d0772309f9b3879fbbb2d3f4008d6f97ed580da 7928062332ebd43e587f6cbbb710dcd1b4f7df6c && git checkout -B drift-repro 9d0772309f9b3879fbbb2d3f4008d6f97ed580da && git merge --no-ff 7928062332ebd43e587f6cbbb710dcd1b4f7df6c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9d0772309f9b3879fbbb2d3f4008d6f97ed580da
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9d0772309f9b3879fbbb2d3f4008d6f97ed580da` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review brief — PR #35865 @ `e8cc0cb24d0b8649b798af2e83548086fd9a9af6` (card #35492)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #35492: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #35865: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `e8cc0cb24d0b8649b798af2e83548086fd9a9af6`
  · the check-runs on `e8cc0cb24d0b8649b798af2e83548086fd9a9af6`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f6f2f87a-1f68-5b6b-ba36-b37fd0636732/scratchpad/d7d/pr-35865/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## L1: REWORK at `e8cc0cb24d0b8649b798af2e83548086fd9a9af6` (2026-11-20T14:23Z): one small code item, two records, CI

This review covers the PR's 33 files against merge base `e1143241d` (+2,315 / −19). Dev report: 7041766952. Claim: 7038675232.

The engine, the CLI, the REST door, the remedy and the destructive findings hold. One operator-facing sentence is false, and two records are owed.

### What I checked

**The mapping and the targets.**
- `unitCodeMappingOf` refuses `VALIDATION_ERROR` on `mapping` in three cases: the mapping is not an object, a key is white space only (the blank key is spelled `""`), or a target is blank. ✔
- Targets are judged before any read, for a standard target or a scoped organization. With no organization named, an organization code is judged after the read-only preview, against each organization in `targetsByOrganization`, and before any write. ✔
- `judgeTarget` refuses three ways, all `INVALID_FIELD` on the code field: not a member, a retired unit, or another dimension. ✔

**Membership matches the write check.**
- `OrganizationUnits.verdict` and U5's `membershipOf` both use `standardUnitOf`, an exact own-key lookup, and then the organization's `sys_unit` rows. Nothing is folded.
- So a value the run counts as `unmatched` is exactly a value the write check answers `ERR_UNIT_CODE_UNKNOWN`. The remedy never points at a run that would skip the row. ✔

**Q2 (A), stored codes left as stored.**
- A retired code and a code of another dimension count as members and are skipped.
- In `assertUnitCodes` the remedy is appended only on the `REQUIRED` and `UNKNOWN` arms, and only when `!codeWritten`. The `RETIRED` and `DIMENSION_MISMATCH` arms carry no remedy.
- So no refusal names a door that leaves its row untouched. I agree with A. ✔

**The `""` entry and blanks.**
- A blank beside a non-blank quantity is written only when `has('')`. Otherwise it is counted as `blankBesideQuantity` and left.
- A blank with no quantity is counted as `skippedBlank`.
- `has` is `hasOwnProperty`, so a `__proto__` or `toString` stored value cannot hit an inherited key. ✔

**Apply.**
- The run counts first and is refused on `unmatched > 0` before any write.
- Each row is written through `engine.update` under `{ isSystem, tenantId }`.
- The write check judges organization codes by the row image's organization (`organizationOf`), so an all-organizations apply is judged per row. ✔
- A row that fails goes to `failures` through the shared `rowFailureSentence`, which is now exported from `record-currency-backfill.ts` with no change to its body. ✔

**Scope.**
- One organization, or every organization explicitly.
- An unscoped run over more than one named organization is refused with each organization's counts.
- Naming an organization on an object with no `organization_id` is refused `INVALID_FIELD`, the same as the currency twin's refusal. ✔

**CLI.**
- The map file is parsed and judged by `unitCodeMappingOf` before the occupancy probe, the prompt and the boot.
- Confirmation and exit behaviour follow `record-currency-codes`.
- The family pins are extended: confirmation exit, JSON stdout purity, and the one-shot family. ✔

**REST.**
- The body key set is closed. `organizationId` and `allOrganizations` get their own sentence.
- `setup.write` is asked first, then the current organization (403 without one), then the guarded dynamic import (501).
- On a 4xx the response carries `details.fields` plus `details.unmatched`.
- Row 50c and its register line mirror row 50b. ✔

**Destructive findings.**
- `unit_mode_to_record` fires on a stored `number` newly in `record` mode, and `unit_mode_to_code` on a stored `text` newly in `code` mode.
- Both are lifted by `force`, both read no row, and both name the CLI command and the REST body.
- The spec change is the `describe` text of `DestructiveChangeIssueSchema.code` only, regenerated into `protocol.mdx`.
- The ADR text records that a re-pointed `unitField` is out of R1. ✔

**Ablations.**
- A (the apply refusal) and B (the member skip) ran at `0d20cb9d6c`.
- The only later engine commit, 416b3f28, is a pure refactor. `tallyValue` now reads `mapping[value]` for `mapped`, where before it took `code`, and that value is the same `mapping[value]`. Neither anchor line moved.
- e8cc0cb2 changes tests only.
- So both ablations stand for the final head. I accept that deviation. ✔

**Changeset classification.**
- `Clause-②: yes` covers the new exports, the new CLI command and the new REST door.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` covers the two `DestructiveChangeIssue` codes.
- Every bump is minor, and `@objectstack/spec` at minor is at least the patch its `describe` bytes need. ✔

### Required

1. **A false ✓ sentence, and the predicate behind it** (`unit-code-backfill.ts`, `formatUnitCodeBackfillReport` and `unitCodeBackfillComplete`).
   - **The problem.** When `mapped === 0 && unmatched === 0`, the report prints `✓ Every <object>.<field> value is a unit code — nothing to convert.`, and `unitCodeBackfillComplete` answers `true`. Both happen even when `blankBesideQuantity > 0`. Those rows hold no unit code, and each one's next quantity edit is refused `ERR_UNIT_CODE_REQUIRED`, whose remedy sends the operator back to this run.
   - **A pin enshrines it.** The idempotence case asserts that exact ✓ line on the second run while `m5` (blank unit, `weight: 5`) is still blank, and the apply case asserts `unitCodeBackfillComplete(report) === true` with `blankBesideQuantity: 1`.
   - **The fix.** Make the ✓ line say only what holds when `blankBesideQuantity > 0`. For example: "Every stored text in … is a unit code; N blank unit(s) beside a quantity remain, refused at their next quantity edit until written, or mapped with a "" entry". Then either count `blankBesideQuantity` in `unitCodeBackfillComplete`, or state in its docblock and the changeset that blanks are outside "complete". Re-pin both cases.
   - **L2.** This item is the L2's to rule alongside Q2. The design that blanks are left unless `""` is mapped stays as it is; what is false is the sentence and the predicate's name for that state.

### Records owed (no new head needed)

2. **Claim amendment.** The diff writes `scripts/check-undeclared-dep-imports.mjs` and `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`, and neither is on claim 7038675232's file surface. Both are gate-forced rows with no behaviour, and the PR body declares them, but each still needs a claim amendment record.
   - Name the three `packages/cli/test/**` and `packages/cli/src/utils/**` family pins in the same record, so that reading them as "their tests" is on file rather than inferred.
3. **Skills-docs.** The follow-up is "noted, not filed": `cli.mdx`'s `os migrate unit-codes` section, the `metadata.endpoints.maintenance` describe in `rest-server.zod.ts` with its generated page, and a units page under `content/docs/data-modeling/` that names the door. File it as a card, and have the PR body's `Skills-docs:` line name that issue before landing.
   - Q1 (the client SDK twin `meta.migrateUnitCodes`): I agree with A, a follow-up card. File it the same way.

### Nit (not blocking)

- N1. The changeset's "A metadata save that declares a unit code field **over stored rows**" reads as if rows were counted. The detector judges a stored field and reads no row, as the ADR note says. Consider "over a stored field (no row is read)".

### Before landing

- **CI green on the final head.** At `e8cc0cb24d` it showed 25 success, 10 skipped, 32 in progress, none red yet.
- **L2.** A CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER PASS on the final head (claim 7041843350). Its three faces are the Clause-② widening, the two protocol codes, and Q2, with item 1 above added.
- **Delta L1.** After item 1.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e8cc0cb24d0b8649b798af2e83548086fd9a9af6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-write-face.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/unit-code-membership.ts, packages/objectql/src/unit-code-backfill.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-unit-code-backfill-route.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/unit-codes.ts

Inputs read: card #35492 (body and its 4 comments: 7035331645, 7037347112, 7038675232, 7041766952), PR #35865 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at this head), the check-runs on this head, and the settlement the card cites (7014013098 on #35469). Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `engine-update.ts` (the U5 call site), `homeAmountOrganizationOf`, `record-currency-backfill.ts`, ADR-0158 L1 and Open items 8, 9, 12, AGENTS.md Prime Directive 5.

Check-runs on this head, read twice (last at 67 runs): no run has failed. Completed and green: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, Build Docs, Check Documentation Links, Lint & Repo Gates and every Lint lane, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger. Still in progress when this record was rendered: Build Core, Test Core 1 to 10, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, the UI lanes. Those verdicts are the gates' own and are not judged here; convergence is the seat's.

### ① Derived judgments

- `DestructiveChangeIssueSchema.code` describe now lists `unit_mode_to_record` and `unit_mode_to_code`. Right: `code` stays `z.string()`, so no accept set moves; the describe names exactly the two codes `detectDestructiveObjectChanges` emits, and the generated `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` row carries the same sentence.
- New 409 `DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE` findings on an object save. Right as a widening, not a narrowing: the saves they refuse declare `unitConfig`, and `unitConfig` is unpublished (`.changeset/35489-unit-config.md` is still pending on `main`, spec at 18.6.0; release pairing ruled on 7037347112). No published accept set loses a member. `force: true` lifts both.
- New public surface, each right for what it is: `@objectstack/objectql` exports `backfillUnitCodes`, `formatUnitCodeBackfillReport`, `unitCodeBackfillComplete`, `unitCodeMappingOf` and six types, and newly exports `rowFailureSentence` from its module only (not from the index); `@objectstack/cli` gains `os migrate unit-codes`; `@objectstack/rest` gains `POST /api/v1/meta/_migrate-unit-codes` behind `metadata.endpoints.maintenance` and `setup.write`, with a closed body set.
- `ERR_UNIT_CODE_REQUIRED` and `ERR_UNIT_CODE_UNKNOWN` messages gain a trailing remedy when the code field was not in the write. Right: no code, status or field moves, and the remedy prints the object and field only, never the resting value, so the module's rule that a resting code is named by its field alone still holds.
- No error code is new: the door answers `INVALID_FIELD`, `VALIDATION_ERROR` and `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`, all 400 or the object-not-found answer. Right.
- The route ledger row is `server-only`. Right for this PR: `packages/client` is outside the claimed file surface.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes

The changeset bumps `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/spec` at `minor`, with `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: added` on both the PR body and the changeset. That matches what the diff publishes: new exports, a new command, a new route, two added finding codes, and nothing removed or narrowed against a published release (see ①). `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` for a describe-only edit is the added-code level the `Metadata-protocol: added` line names. Check Changeset is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev open question 1 (SDK twin `meta.migrateUnitCodes`): answered A, as a follow-up card for the seat to file. The currency door has its SDK method, and the `server-only` ledger row is correct only until that card lands. Not a blocker here.
- Dev open question 2 (a stored retired code, or a code of another dimension, left as stored and counted `member`): answered A, as built. ADR-0158 L1 keeps a resting row's code ("Old rows keep their code and stored conversion"), and settlement point 5 exists so that one apply run converts the field; option B would refuse every apply run on a field with one retired unit until the operator re-means historic rows. It is a reading of settlement points 4 and 5, whose literal "member" in U5's own first sentence excludes a retired unit, so the ADR-0158 amendment must state it. The `adr_amendment` text in 7041766952 does. See N2 for the label.
- Dev deviation: no finding for a re-pointed `unitField` or a narrowed `unitDimension`. Disclosed in the PR's acceptance notes; the re-point half is the same hole as S1 and is answered there.
- Dev deviations on gate-forced rows outside the claim surface (`scripts/check-undeclared-dep-imports.mjs`, `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 50c): accepted, each is a ledger row with no behaviour; row 50c matches the route's `isSystem` read.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` (cli.mdx, the `maintenance` describe in `rest-server.zod.ts`, a units page): noted for the seat; the `rest-server.zod.ts` describe names the doors the switch mounts and is stale until that follow-up lands.
- SQL push-down: `walkUnitCodes` reads every row of the object in pages of 500, joins each stored value to `sys_unit` in the application (a per-page `$in` read into a cache) and tallies distinct values in the application, where SQL could `GROUP BY` the column and anti-join the unit table. The module gives no reason of its own. A reason exists and holds: the settlement requires exact matching (`kg`, `KG` and `kg ` are three keys), which a database collation does not guarantee (case-insensitive and pad-space collations merge them), and the blank test is the precedent's stated reason (`record-currency-backfill.ts`: null comparison is where drivers diverge). The per-row `engine.update` needs each id by design, so U5 judges every converted code. No finding on correctness; the missing sentence is N1.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`** (hits). The describe holds against its first consumer: the two codes it adds are the two `protocol-write-face.ts` pushes, spelled the same, on the same 409 face, beside `currency_mode_to_record`. It holds against 7035331645 point 2 only as far as the detector does; see S1.

**`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-write-face.ts`** (implementing).

S1 (should-fix) — the finding is keyed on the field that carries `unitConfig`, not on the field whose stored text falls under U5, so a save that declares a unit code field over stored rows can pass with no finding. The loop skips a field absent from the previous definition (`if (!prevField) continue; // brand-new field`), and `unit_mode_to_record` requires `isStored(prevField)` on the quantity. Scenario: an object stores `uom` (text, free text in its rows); a save adds a NEW quantity `net_weight` with `unitConfig: { unitMode: 'record', unitField: 'uom' }`. No finding is raised. From that save on `unitCodeSources` makes `uom` a unit code field: every write of `uom` is judged by point 1 of the write check and free text is refused, and `net_weight` cannot be set on an old row until `uom` holds a code. That is the case 7035331645 point 2 carries ("the metadata save that declares `unitConfig` over stored free text answers a destructive-change finding") and the changeset's own sentence ("A metadata save that declares a unit code field over stored rows is a destructive change"), and the code does not keep it. The test `raises nothing for ... a new field` covers only an object where the code field is new too. The disclosed re-pointed `unitField` case is the same hole: the newly named stored column becomes a code field with no finding. The same keying also over-fires: a `text` field already named by a stored `record` quantity, then marked `unitMode: 'code'`, raises `unit_mode_to_code` though nothing changes for its rows. Fix shape: judge the stored code field, as the write check does, by comparing `unitCodeSources(prev.fields)` with `unitCodeSources(next.fields)`: a stored `text` field that is a source after the save and was not before raises the finding, whichever declaration made it one; keep the quantity-keyed finding for the blank-beside-quantity debt. Pin the new-quantity case and the re-point case.

Otherwise the detector agrees with its contract: it reads no row, an unstored previous field raises nothing, `fixed` and a removed declaration raise nothing, `force` lifts both, and each message names the run for the object and the code field (the `unitField`, not the quantity), CLI and REST, matching `unitCodeBackfillRemedy` in objectql.
